queries.sql:
WITH account_scope AS (
 SELECT b."ownerId" AS owner_id
 FROM bots b JOIN coordinator_bots c ON c."botId"=b.id AND c."ownerId"=b."ownerId" AND c."workspaceId"=b."workspaceId"
 WHERE b.id='d51efc47-1c61-4758-8c05-fd7a07e3d7b2' AND b."workspaceId"='4ae2a643-b09e-43eb-816c-1e5557bef170'
)
SELECT f.id AS task_id, f.revision, f.stage, f.status, i.scope AS issue_scope,
 b."workspaceId" AS task_workspace_id,
 EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM mikka_workspace_members m WHERE m."workspaceId"=b."workspaceId" AND m."userId"=f."userId" AND m.status='active') AS task_workspace_active_membership,
 (SELECT w.id FROM mikka_workspaces w WHERE w."userId"=f."userId" AND w.kind='personal' LIMIT 1)='4ae2a643-b09e-43eb-816c-1e5557bef170' AS personal_issue_scope_matches_preflight,
 f."candidateId" IS NULL AS candidate_is_null
FROM factory_tasks f JOIN account_scope s ON s.owner_id=f."userId"
 JOIN issues i ON i.id=f."issueId"
 JOIN bots b ON b.id=f."botId" AND b."ownerId"=f."userId"
WHERE f.id='b2e96bca-9287-4ed7-92e7-68d9b8a3285f'
SELECT count(*)::integer AS matching_workspace_rows FROM mikka_workspaces WHERE id IN ('4ae2a643-b09e-43eb-816c-1e5557bef170','de300001-ece6-4021-8214-c986ea306bde')

interpretation: The same historical task remained revision 3, execute/blocked, with a null candidate.
Its Bot workspace differs from the authenticated preflight workspace, and the owner has an active membership in that persisted task workspace.
The actual issue scope is workspace. The personal_issue_scope_matches_preflight column only tests this owner's personal workspace ID; it does not say the historical issue is personal.
The default database contains neither of these workspace IDs. No production DATABASE_URL or connection string was read, so this is not an environment-binding receipt.
The authenticated Factory detail must still return matching task identity/revision and a non-null other liveWorkspaceId before the acceptance driver can continue.
Read-only statements were separate snapshots. No task, configuration, profile or run was modified.
